slices.title: floor check treats NULL segment as unknown - declared detection change

decision.question: How should c_issue_size_floor treat a NULL segment - judge it against the stricter (MAINBOARD) floor, or raise a separate finding?
decision.answer: NEITHER judge it against the stricter floor NOR let it fail silently: a NULL segment is EXCLUDED from the segment-floor check and raises its own distinct, named finding.
decision.decidedFrom: docs/design/data-sourcing-pull-model.md line 812 (the INVITS/REITS row) and line 703 (the pe_at_floor/_cap row) - the design text, not convenience, as instructed.
decision.evidence812: "segment is NULL for all 5 today ... Out of the pull model first release - SAY SO EXPLICITLY RATHER THAN LETTING THEM FAIL EVERY CHECK." That is the design ruling directly on a NULL segment: an unknown must not be silently judged by a rule that does not apply to it.
decision.evidence703: "null with pe_not_ascertainable_reason when loss-making - never 0 ... the reason column is 0% populated, so today not-ascertainable is indistinguishable from not-extracted." The general principle: unknown is legitimate, but it MUST carry a reason, or it collapses into missing.
decision.consequence: 2-S3c therefore: (a) c_issue_size_floor skips rows with a NULL segment rather than applying the MAINBOARD floor; (b) a separate named finding counts them, so they stay VISIBLE rather than quietly excluded; (c) the provenance reason is mandatory, per line 703, otherwise unknown becomes indistinguishable from never-looked.

evidence: filing-persister.ts:437 says it outright: "W-147 provenance marker, not data - it ranks the cover headline below a price band ad (see coverOutrankedByAd)".

coverOutrankedByAd:600 opens with `if (!isCoverHeadline) return false;` and isCoverHeadline:597 is `str(extraction, "headline_source") === "PROSPECTUS_COVER"`. For any non-cover source it returns false - never drops.

s7RulingOverturned.theRealState: ipo_details has NO general source-priority mechanism. The matrix does not rank it (my correction, confirmed). dropOutranked does not rank it (this correction). filterFields is admin-protection, not ranking. So a report-82 write would carry NO source ranking - which is exactly the "209th field with no priority resolution" objection I raised originally and then WITHDREW for a bad reason.

s7RulingOverturned.myOwnErrorInThisChain: I raised the no-priority-resolution objection FIRST, then withdrew it when I accepted that #367 matrix entry supplied ranking. That was my error (the matrix governs ipos only). The peer then replaced it with the dropOutranked argument, also wrong. So doing the 531-row re-key as a SQL UPDATE through the SQL twin would collapse EVERY junk-name row under one IPO to the empty string, they would collide with each other under E1, and lane A s8b would fire on all of them. The re-key must run in TypeScript.

blankKeyMeasurement.prod: normalized_name is ABSENT on all three tables in ipodhan. Rows 27/326/178 = 531 - which is exactly where the 531 figure comes from, but the COLUMN IS NOT THERE. E1 on prod is therefore a bigger step than on staging: add column, backfill, then constrain.
blankKeyMeasurement.staging: Column PRESENT on all three. Rows 29/321/194 = 544.
blankKeyMeasurement.answer: ZERO blank keys on all three tables. There is no blank-key collision on current data, so E1 does NOT need to be a partial unique index to apply. The 0/0/5 baseline reproduces exactly and independently, and the 5 are precisely the two-role banks named: ICICI Bank x2, Kotak Mahindra Bank, Axis Bank, Centrum Broking.
blankKeyMeasurement.butNotSafeForever: Zero today is not zero forever. The column is notNull default empty and rowKeyForName returns null for a blank name, which the backfill SKIPS - so a future blank-name row lands as the empty string. Two of those under one IPO make a plain UNIQUE reject the second write at RUNTIME, mid-extraction. That is a live-write failure, not a migration failure, and no amount of measuring today prevents it.
blankKeyMeasurement.recommendation: PLAIN UNIQUE, not partial - and fix it at the writer instead. rowKeyForName returning null already means the row has no identity and the design says the caller MUST skip writing it. A partial index WHERE normalized_name <> the empty string would silently permit unlimited blank-name rows, which is exactly the duplication E1 exists to stop, just invisible - and it would mask a writer that failed to skip. Better: keep the plain UNIQUE and have item 1 writer assert the skip before the database sees the row, so the failure is early and legible rather than a constraint violation mid-extraction.

sqlTwinAttempt.fault1: NESTING ORDER INVERTED. In nested REGEXP_REPLACE the INNERMOST call runs FIRST. The emitted SQL was LOWER(TRIM(REGEXP_REPLACE( x16 then $1 AS norm - every static chunk after ${input} vanished, giving syntax error at or near AS. The source template is complete and closes correctly, so this is about how the nested sql`` value composes, not a typo. NOT diagnosed; the next attempt should dump the queryChunks before running anything against a database.

sqlTwinDone.rootCause: The SHELL was collapsing doubled backslashes inside my heredocs, so the generated file carried SINGLE backslashes where a TypeScript template literal needs DOUBLE. JS silently eats a lone backslash, so every pattern was quietly wrong - and a single-backslash backreference is an ILLEGAL OCTAL ESCAPE in a template literal, which truncated the emitted SQL and produced the syntax-error-at-AS I could not explain. One cause, both faults.
sqlTwinDone.howItWasFixed: Never write a literal backslash in the generator - chr(92) throughout - and ASSERT the result before running anything: 14 doubled-s escapes, 3 doubled-y, 1 doubled-1, and ZERO lone backslashes in the new block. That assertion could have failed, which is the only reason it was worth writing.
sqlTwinDone.secondFaultAlsoReal: The inverted nesting was genuine and is fixed: the innermost REGEXP_REPLACE runs FIRST, so the chain is now built inside-out.
sqlTwinDone.shape: 14 steps against about 20 nested levels before. Ten end-anchored suffix replaces collapse into ONE Postgres word-bounded replace; the paren and hyphen folds move above it.

slice12DDesignConflict.cardSays: 12-S6: a non-empty CIN matching exactly one row WINS over a disagreeing name match and logs identity_conflict; CIN is tier 0, above ISIN.
slice12DDesignConflict.whatTheCodeActuallyDoes: ipo-identity.ts:485 resolves a key-versus-name disagreement as: const resolution = nameMatchIsTier3b ? keyMatch : nameMatch. So when the name match came from TIER 3 (exact or compact-whitespace name), the NAME MATCH WINS over the key match. That is deliberate and annotated: T-403 Tier-A review item 4 says tier 3 keeps the pre-T-318 behaviour because that is what every existing caller relied on.
slice12DDesignConflict.theConflict: If CIN is added as another keyMatch source - the obvious reading of "tier 0, above ISIN" - it does NOT win against an exact name match. It LOSES, by that same line. The card requirement is unreachable by adding a tier.
slice12DDesignConflict.andAShortCircuitDoesNotWorkEither: Returning immediately on a unique CIN hit would make CIN win, but the card ALSO requires logging identity_conflict when CIN disagrees with a name match - and you cannot know a disagreement exists without running the name tiers. So a pure short-circuit cannot satisfy the card either.
slice12DDesignConflict.whatItActuallyRequires: 12-D must introduce a precedence distinction so a CIN key match outranks a name match while ISIN and symbol still do not - i.e. modify line 485, the single most-reviewed line in the module (T-403 Tier-A review item 4, guarding behaviour every existing caller depends on). That is a Tier A change to the most-guarded logic in the identity path, not "add a tier".
slice12DDesignConflict.theTradeToWeigh: Combined with the sizing: this modification would be made to benefit the 9.6% of rows that carry a CIN. Changing the most-reviewed guard in the identity module to serve one row in ten is a trade the owner or the design should weigh explicitly, not something to improvise at build time.
slice12DDesignConflict.whatIsStillCleanlyBuildable: The duplicate-candidate half (former 12-S5) does NOT touch line 485 at all - it appends a structured log after the tier chain and returns the row unchanged. It is buildable on its own, it carries the real value per the sizing (13 candidate groups on staging, 0 on prod), and it has real fixtures. If the CIN decision takes time, that half should not wait behind it.

slice12D1.safetyProperty: The scan runs BEFORE the tier chain and is awaited for its side effect only. It reads nothing the tiers produce and feeds nothing back, so it CANNOT alter the returned row however it behaves. Placing it after the chain would have meant threading it past three separate return statements, and the first thing to go wrong there is a return that skips it.
slice12D1.failureContainment: It swallows its own failures - every scraper write depends on resolveIpoRow, so an observation must never break it. Pinned by a test that rejects the scan and asserts resolution still returns the right row, and another that deletes the repository method entirely.
slice12D1.flagDecision: Plain === true, deliberately NOT slotAwareFlagDefault(), which returns true on staging when unset. The card says default false in EVERY slot. Pinned by a test that sets DEPLOY_SLOT=staging and asserts the scan is not even queried. I gave a builder the wrong helper on this exact point once before; this time I read feature-flags.ts:64 first rather than trusting memory.
slice12D1.queryShape: findLiveByOpenDate is date-FILTERED rather than fetch-all-live-rows: a same-day query returns a handful, where a full live scan would cost an O(n) fold on EVERY identity resolution - and identity resolution runs on every scraped record.
slice12D1.proof: 9 new tests; the pre-existing 39-test identity suite passes UNCHANGED; tsc exit code 0 - gated on tsc own exit code after I caught my command printing CLEAN off a piped tail exit status; mutation - requiring three matches instead of two turns exactly the log test red, restored to 9 of 9.

slice12ESizing.verdict: BUILDABLE and a genuine improvement, but the carded chain is half dead and the cost is 4 named IPOs. Measured before building; read-only, zero writes.
slice12ESizing.deadTiers: The card says the chain is symbol then ISIN then exact normalized name. The InvestorGain source provides NEITHER a symbol NOR an ISIN - I listed every field it returns. So the first TWO tiers have nothing to match on and provide zero safety for this source. Anyone reading the card would think there are three fallbacks; there is one.
slice12ESizing.howOftenFuzzyFires: The 0.6-similarity path only runs when two IPOs share BOTH dates - and that is the NORM, not an edge case: 194 of 333 production rows (58%) sit in a shared open+close date group, because SME issues routinely share a window. 83 such groups on staging, 69 on prod.
slice12ESizing.theRealMeasurement: Took the 29 real records from the captured GMP fixture, normalised their clean ~ipo_name, and matched against every staging company name: 24 bind to exactly ONE row, ZERO are ambiguous, 5 match nothing.
slice12ESizing.whatTheFiveAre: One is junk - a header row whose name is literally "NSE" - and should be filtered regardless. FOUR are real IPOs that would stop showing GMP: Jindal Supreme, Steamhouse, Asset Reconstruction, Glass Wall Systems. In each the source uses a SHORTER name than the database, e.g. source "Asset Reconstruction" against stored "ASSET RECONSTRUCTION COMPANY (INDIA) LIMITED" which binds to "asset reconstruction india".
slice12ESizing.theInterestingPart: ZERO ambiguous matches. The fuzzy path exists to pick the best of several date matches, but exact name is already UNIQUE wherever it matches at all. So strict binding is not merely safer - it is more decisive than the thing it replaces. The 0.6 threshold is doing worse work than an exact key would.
slice12ESizing.cost: 4 of 28 real records - about 14% - lose their GMP display until their names align. That is a visible, user-facing cost and it must be in the PR body by NAME, not as a percentage.
slice12ESizing.doNotFixItWithTheFold: The obvious patch is to bind on foldCompanyIdentity, which strips "india" and would match all four. That is wrong: the fold is deliberately COARSER and is the key a row-DELETING repair uses. Widening the binding key to the fold would merge companies that differ only by a country word. The four are a data-alignment issue to track, not a reason to loosen the key.

slice12E.design: The decision is extracted into a PURE exported chooseListBinding - no database, no logging, no I/O - mirroring computeGMPRunOutcome in the same file. matchIPOByDates was never exported and so could never be unit-tested; the decision now can be, exhaustively, without a connection.
slice12E.cardCorrection: The card specified symbol then ISIN then exact name. The source provides NEITHER a symbol NOR an ISIN, so only the last tier exists here. The PR body says so rather than implying three safety nets.
slice12E.costNamed: Four records stop showing GMP until their stored names align with the source shorter form: Jindal Supreme, Steamhouse, Asset Reconstruction, Glass Wall Systems. Named in the body, not given as a percentage.
slice12E.scopeHeld: The plus-or-minus one day date tolerance was left alone. The card asked for the similarity path only, and widening to unmeasured behaviour is how a slice grows a defect.
slice12E.unreachableHandledAnyway: UNBOUND is handled explicitly in the caller even though it is unreachable there. An invariant the compiler cannot see is exactly the kind that stops being true after an edit.
slice12E.detectionDeclaration: No detection change, with the reason: the slice only NARROWS what is written and sits behind a flag off in every slot, so it cannot introduce a new wrong-write class, only decline writes it previously made.
slice12E.proof: 9 new tests including both directions of the flag on identical input - off binds a merely-similar name, on refuses it. Existing orchestrator suite unchanged, 13 of 13 together. Zero type errors in this file; main carries 99 pre-existing scraper errors and this adds none.

closingChain.singleCause: All four are the COUNTRY WORD. Jindal Supreme vs Jindal Supreme (India) Ltd.; Steamhouse vs Steamhouse India Ltd.; Asset Reconstruction vs ASSET RECONSTRUCTION COMPANY (INDIA) LIMITED; Glass Wall Systems vs Glass Wall Systems (India) Limited. The source omits India, we store it, nothing else differs.
closingChain.closingFixMeasured: Dropping the country word from the BINDING key: production 333 names, identities 333 to 333, ZERO newly merged groups. Staging 376 names, 349 to 349, ONE newly merged group - the ARCIL pair, which is the same company and the merge 12-B exists to make. Zero false merges across 709 real names.
closingChain.whyThisDoesNotContradictMyWarning: I warned against fixing it with foldCompanyIdentity and that still stands. The FOLD strips india AND and/the/of/company AND compacts away every space - far wider, and it is the key a row-DELETING repair uses. Dropping ONLY the country word is a much narrower change and it measures clean. The distinction is the point, not a walk-back.
closingChain.chain: 12-E as-is: 4 unbound. Plus the country-word drop: 1. Plus 12-C duplicate repair: 0.
closingChain.theLastOne: Asset Reconstruction is AMBIGUOUS rather than unmatched - staging carries two rows that both reduce to the same key, which is the genuine duplicate pair. It resolves when that duplicate is repaired, which is already 12-C job. No new slice needed.
closingChain.whereItShips: Folding the country-word drop into 12-B rather than opening a seventh branch: it touches the same function in the same file 12-B already changes, and shipping it separately would re-key the same 544 rows twice. slice12D2Deferred.whyThatSettlesIt: Making a key tier outrank an exact-name match means changing ipo-identity.ts:485 - const resolution = nameMatchIsTier3b ? keyMatch : nameMatch - which is annotated T-403 review item 4 and pinned by the identity suite conflict cases. stagingProof.toolVerdict: HELD: violation count stayed 0 across 2 distinct scraper cycles
stagingProof.caveat: THE ASSERTION IS WEAKER THAN ITS EXIT CODE READS, and I am recording that rather than banking it. The two cycles it observed advanced the scraper_logs marker only. The repaired tables were NOT written by them: promoters and ipo_intermediaries last changed 2026-09-09T16:48Z, peer_companies 2026-06-17. A cycle that never touches the repaired rows cannot refute the repair.
stagingProof.toolBehaviourUnderstood: Two false alarms of my own, both checked and withdrawn. (1) The marker timestamps looked 5h30m in the future; they are the known stored-timestamp skew - staging labels rows ~5.5h behind real time - not a tool bug. (2) I nearly called the whole proof invalid on that basis. Watching the marker for 90s settled it: logs_marker moved 12:46:30 -> 12:48:28 within 50 seconds of real time, so the advances the tool counted were REAL.
stagingProof.whatWouldMakeItStrong: A cycle that actually writes a promoter, peer or intermediary row - those come from document/filing extraction, not from every wake. Until one lands, the honest state is: repair applied, invariant independently clean, survived two cycles that did not exercise the write path at risk.
stagingProof.status: UNVERIFIABLE (write path not exercised) - never PASS
stagingProof.writePathNamed: PRICE_BAND_AD extraction, measured by lane B (#545): on staging RHP/DRHP extraction has NEVER written a promoter or peer; only PBA extraction writes promoters (7 of 14 completed PBAs). peer_companies 321 rows are one 2026-06-17 backfill. The last promoter row (2026-09-09 16:48:00.138Z) IS the last PBA extraction instant. So no repair was at fault and NO cycle count would ever have exercised those tables.
stagingProof.reassertWhen: The next PRICE_BAND_AD extraction on staging - it arrives when a new IPO price-band ad is ingested and cannot be forced. Re-assert then, asserting the table gained a row with updated_at AFTER the repair.

structuralArgument.claim: A stale row key cannot be RE-INTRODUCED by any write path, because every writer of the three repaired tables computes the key through ONE function - rowKeyForName in packages/shared/src/utils/company-name-normalizer.ts, the exact file 12-B changed. There is no second implementation.
structuralArgument.writersEnumerated: FOUR, all verified by reading them: filing-persister.ts:1378 (intermediaries), :1679 (peers), :1741 (promoters) - all three call rowKeyForName; and web/lib/repositories/peer-company-repository.ts:102, a SEPARATE web-side writer I went looking for specifically because a second path is where this kind of repair usually leaks. It calls the same rowKeyForName and its own comment says so.
structuralArgument.whatThisChanges: Item 12 moves from "waiting blindly on an event nobody can force" to "structurally sound, awaiting empirical confirmation". The missing PBA extraction would CONFIRM what the code structure says must be true; it is no longer the only thing standing between the repair and confidence.
structuralArgument.whatItIsNOT: NOT a substitute for the contract real-data proof. A structural argument proves the source shares one implementation; it does not prove the deployed artifact is that source, and it cannot catch a path that writes these columns by raw SQL outside the repositories. Recording the limit with the argument.

creationPathAnswered.question: lane B asked which source wrote the 2026-09-09 short-name row, and whether a third row could still be created before the E1 constraint is applied on production.
creationPathAnswered.answer: CHITTORGARH created it, alone. All 16 of the dropped row field_sources rows are CHITTORGARH and its only DONE pipeline step is F6/CHITTORGARH. The kept row is multi-source: DRHP 46, BSE 8, ADMIN 2, NSE 1, CHITTORGARH 1.
creationPathAnswered.mechanism: Chittorgarh publishes the name as "Asset Reconstruction Co.(India) Ltd." while the stored row is "ASSET RECONSTRUCTION COMPANY (INDIA) LIMITED". Under the pre-12-B normaliser those did not fold together, identity resolution missed, and the scraper INSERTED a new IPO row instead of matching the existing one.
creationPathAnswered.whyItMattersNow: PROVEN AGAINST THE CURRENT CODE: both names now fold to "asset reconstruction" under the post-12-B normaliser. So 12-B DEMONSTRABLY PREVENTS THIS EXACT DUPLICATE CLASS, evidenced by a real duplicate that actually occurred on 2026-09-09 rather than by a constructed test.
creationPathAnswered.sequencingAnswer: So the answer to lane B sequencing question is: NO, a third row cannot be created by this path once 12-B is deployed, because identity resolution now matches before the insert is reached. The E1 unique constraint is defence-in-depth here, not the primary guard - which means the constraint does NOT have to precede the production backfill.
creationPathAnswered.sideFinding: The dropped row document_fetch_state is BLOCKED_ALL on all 7 attempts, which is why it has zero documents. That connects to the correlation measured earlier: a Chittorgarh-only row with no BSE identifier cannot fetch documents at all.

planRecut.outcome: REVIEWED, NO CHANGE. Five slices stay five. Consolidating would make the item worse, not faster.
whyNoMerge: 3-S1 + 3-S2 is the only real merge candidate (~430, over the band) and it MIXES TIERS: 3-S1 deletes 27 unreachable keys and is provably a no-op by deep-equal snapshot; 3-S2 changes the rules deciding live writes for 16 fields. Folding a provable no-op into a live-write change buries the safe half inside a Tier A review.

3-S3 is blocked on lane A item 1 being DONE on main - it must be written against item 1 FINAL call sites, and the plan says a rebase there is a real conflict, not a textual one. It cannot be merged into an earlier slice that is not blocked.
3-S4 is a repair tool that DELETES rows. Same reasoning as item 12 12-C: a data deletion stays its own slice with its own dry-run evidence rather than buried inside a code review.
3-S5 is a detection change with its own registry entry and regenerated aggregate. Merging it into a code slice would mix a CI/detection change with a behaviour change.
planRecut.keptOrdering: The plan already orders the three matrix hunks so none overlaps - 3-S1 deletions only, 3-S2 additions only, 3-S3 the two function bodies only. That ordering is the thing preventing conflicting hunks in one file and is preserved.

slice3S1Blocked.status: NOT BUILT - the plan card is WRONG and building it as written would have shipped a silent defect
slice3S1Blocked.planClaim: 3-S1: "Delete the 27 unreachable snake_case keys", deletions only, "proven a no-op by deep-equal snapshot", Tier B.
slice3S1Blocked.whatIMeasured: getFieldRules(fieldName) resolves in this order: toCamelKey(fieldName) first, then the RAW fieldName, then DEFAULT_RULES. So a snake_case key is unreachable ONLY when a camelCase sibling exists - the camel entry wins first. With no sibling, the raw snake key is found by the second lookup and IS returned.
slice3S1Blocked.counts: The matrix has 77 top-level keys: 27 snake_case, 50 camelCase. Of the 27 snake keys only FIVE have a camelCase sibling and are therefore genuinely unreachable: company_description, open_date, close_date, lot_size, gmp_price. The other TWENTY-TWO have no camelCase equivalent at all, so deleting them does not remove a duplicate - it removes the only entry, and those fields fall through to DEFAULT_RULES.
slice3S1Blocked.runtimeEvidence: Ground truth from field_sources, read-only. Staging carries live snake_case provenance rows for names on the not-safe list: profit_fy1 155 rows, profit_fy2 123, profit_fy3 3, revenue_fy1 23, revenue_fy2 9, revenue_fy3 3, roe_percentage 123. Production carries none of these yet (its only snake name is PRICE_BAND_AD, a document type, not a matrix field). So the deletion is not hypothetical on staging - it would change how at least seven financial fields resolve their source priority.
slice3S1Blocked.whatWouldHaveHappened: Deleting all 27 as the card instructs would silently move revenue, profit and return-ratio fields onto DEFAULT_RULES - a different source ranking - while the PR body claimed a proven no-op. The deep-equal snapshot the card proposes would have PASSED, because a snapshot of getFieldRules over the matrix keys never asks what happens to a name that is no longer a key.
slice3S1Blocked.theConflation: The card treats "snake_case key" as a synonym for "duplicate of a camelCase key". For 5 of them that is true. For 22 it is false. The acceptance criterion even names "the 5 Group-A camelCase siblings", so the card knew there were five siblings and still said twenty-seven deletions.
slice3S1Blocked.correctScope: 3-S1 deletes the FIVE keys that genuinely have camelCase siblings, and proves it with the deep-equal snapshot the card asks for - which for those five IS a true no-op. issue515.title: price_range holds the FACE VALUE on 6 IPO rows; 5 of 6 also have an unsourced segment
issue515.measured: Read-only, zero writes. face_value = price_range_max AND price_band_high IS NULL: prod 5 of 277 IPO rows, staging 6 of 323.
issue515.theAssociation: 5 of those 6 ALSO have no field_sources provenance for segment. Base rate of unsourced segment is 31 of 322, about 9.6 percent, so independence predicts roughly 0.6 overlapping rows and five were observed. That is one ingestion path that populated neither field, not separate bugs.
issue515.exception: STALLION INDIA FLUOROCHEMICALS is the only one of the six whose segment IS sourced (Chittorgarh). Its story is different and must not be folded into the segment work.
issue515.whyItMattersForItem14: computeBSEIssueSize(shares, band.min) multiplies by the band minimum. When the band minimum IS the face value, issue_size comes out understated by roughly real_price divided by face_value. Item 14 conversion arithmetic is correct and is being fed the wrong price. That is very likely why two of the three c_issue_size_floor violations are rows from this list.
issue515.consequenceForOtherSlices: PIYUSH is NOT in this class (price_range_max 668 is not its face value 10), so it stays item 14 own 10,490-share class. But NIRBHAY sits in BOTH this class and the unsourced-segment class, so repairing its segment alone will NOT make c_issue_size_floor go GONE for it. 2-S3b ledger line must say the floor signal for NIRBHAY is gated on #515 too, or it promises something the repair cannot deliver.
issue515.doNotRepair: No repair until the real price bands are read from a source. A guessed band would be WORSE than the current wrong one because it would look sourced - the same argument that keeps the 33 unreachable segment rows unwritten.
issue515.unmeasured: lot times price_max is Rs1,000 for NIRBHAY and Rs40,000 for STALLION, both outside the mainboard retail window, so these rows may also trip d_lot_band_window. NOT checked. Recorded as a thread, not a finding.

lotBandThreadClosed.wasRecordedAs: unmeasured thread, explicitly not a finding
lotBandThreadClosed.nowMeasured: d_lot_band_window FAILS on staging with 13 violations. THREE are rows from the #515 class and they fail for exactly this cause: NIRBHAY 100 x Rs10 = Rs1,000; STALLION 4000 x Rs10 = Rs40,000; MUTHOOT FINCOTP 100 x Rs1000 = Rs1,00,000 - each against a MAINBOARD retail window of Rs8,000 to Rs20,000, and in each case the price being multiplied IS the face value.
lotBandThreadClosed.whyItWidensTheIssue: The same wrong price degrades TWO independent detection checks, not one: c_issue_size_floor (because computeBSEIssueSize multiplies shares by band.min) and d_lot_band_window (because lot_size times price_range_max uses the same wrong price).
lotBandThreadClosed.consequenceForTheRepair: When #515 is fixed BOTH signals should go GONE for these rows. That is two independent confirmations instead of one - and it means a fix that clears only the issue-size check has not actually fixed the cause.
lotBandThreadClosed.explicitlyNotClaimed: The other 10 d_lot_band_window violations are a different story - WINDLAS 30 x Rs1000, ICICI Prudential AMC 100 x Rs2165, MORGANITE 100 x Rs1557 - all carrying real-looking prices. Either genuine data or a question about the window itself. NOT part of this class and not folded in.

rcaCorrection.whatIGotWrong: I reported that the six #515 rows came from ONE ingestion path, inferring it from the 5-of-6 unsourced-segment overlap. The provenance rows disprove it.
rcaCorrection.measured: BANGANGA and NIRBHAY: priceRangeMax written by BSE, 22 provenance rows each. STALLION: written by CHITTORGARH, 29 rows. MARUTI, MUTHOOT and STANBIK: ZERO field_sources rows for the entire IPO - written by a path that records no provenance at all. Three states, not one.
rcaCorrection.whatStillStands: The association is real and still worth acting on - 5 of 6 also lack a segment source against a base rate of about 9.6%. But same-symptom is not same-writer, and I stated the stronger claim.
rcaCorrection.myError: This was not a measurement problem. I had the overlap number and inferred a common CAUSE from it without checking who actually wrote the field. The check took one query.
rcaCorrection.consequenceFor2S6: A single writer fix cannot close this class. The RCA must name a treatment per state, and one of them is to read the raw BSE payload for BANGANGA and NIRBHAY first - BSE demonstrably serves a real band elsewhere (Price_Band 132.00-139.00 alongside a separate Face_Value 10.00, and bse-api-scraper.ts:267,278-279,295 maps them separately and correctly). So either BSE served a degenerate band for those two or an empty-band path produced it. Undetermined, and not guessed.
rcaCorrection.propagation: Corrected on issue #515 and sent to the delta-2 author, because my wrong inference had already been codified into delta 2 section 4.25.

rcaPrerequisiteBlocked.whatWasAsked: Read the raw BSE payload for BANGANGA and NIRBHAY before concluding anything about BSE band handling - the agreed prerequisite for 2-S6 RCA.
rcaPrerequisiteBlocked.whyItCannotBeDone: Both rows carry NULL bse_ipo_no AND NULL bse_scrip_code. There is no identifier to query the BSE detail endpoint with, so the payload cannot be fetched for either row.
rcaPrerequisiteBlocked.andItIsNotPeculiarToThem: Measured across staging: of 70 rows with ANY field sourced from BSE, only 12 (17.1%) carry a BSE identifier. 58 (82.9%) carry NONE. So the absence is the NORM for BSE-sourced rows, not an anomaly of these two - which also means my first reading, that BSE-attributed rows without a BSE key are contradictory, was wrong.
rcaPrerequisiteBlocked.theBiggerFinding: 83% of BSE-sourced rows cannot be re-fetched from BSE, because the key was never stored. That reaches well beyond #515: for most BSE-sourced rows, ANY value attributed to BSE is unverifiable against its source. A repair that must read the real value from the exchange cannot do so for 5 in 6 of them.
rcaPrerequisiteBlocked.consequenceFor2S6: The RCA cannot be completed by fetching the payload. It needs a different route - recover the identifier by finding the IPO on BSE by name and date, or accept that for these rows the RCA stops at BSE-attributed, unverifiable. That is a design decision, not something to improvise, and it should be recorded on #515 before anyone plans the repair.
rcaPrerequisiteBlocked.notClaimed: I have NOT established why the face value ended up in the price band for these two. That question is now open with a named obstacle rather than a guess.

secondCatch.secondFinding: scraper/src/services/nse-past-issue-matcher.ts EXISTS and is imported NOWHERE - the only reference to it is its own @module docstring. My live probe of both NSE past endpoints failed to fetch from this machine (NSE bot protection; the repo has a whole cookie-priming client for exactly this). So the WALL IS NOT CONFIRMED and neither is the unblock - what is established is that my stated reason for the wall is false.

wallProperlyCharacterised.theWallRESTATED: A BSE-ONLY, CLOSED row with no stored BSE identifier has no reachable source - because BSE is the only exchange that would list it, and BSE publishes only its current board (37 rows). Tested against THREE sources: BSE current board (neither present), Chittorgarh report 82 across four financial years (neither present), NSE public-past-issues 1,431 records (neither present, and correctly so).
wallProperlyCharacterised.whatChanged: My earlier statement - "the exchanges publish only what is currently open" - was BSE-only evidence stated as a plural structural fact, and withdrawing it was right. The CONCLUSION survives with better evidence and a much narrower, testable shape. Both halves matter: the reason was wrong AND the wall is real.
wallProperlyCharacterised.stillOpen: Whether these two rows can be recovered by NAME+DATE against some other archive is untested and I am not claiming it either way.
